answer: Behavioral correlation clustering. Agents log every transaction; the system clusters identities by shared timing, counterparties, and value patterns, then flags clusters whose internal cohesion exceeds organic norms. A flagged cluster has its aggregate reputation diluted proportionally to cluster size, so each fake identity must forge distinct behavioral histories plus sustained diverse interactions—costing roughly the full effort of a genuine agent per identity. Extra identities lose leverage instead of gaining it, and honest gardeners keep full weight while the jade accounts collapse.
